passages.text: ## Step 4: Breaking Down the Concept Further

In a redox reaction, one species is oxidized (loses electrons), and another is reduced (gains electrons). For example, in the reaction between zinc (Zn) and copper(II) sulfate (CuSO4), zinc is oxidized to Zn2+, and Cu2+ is reduced to Cu. In Arabic, this can be described as: "في تفاعل بين الزنك وكبريتات النحاس، يتأكسد الزنك إلى أيون الزنك الموجب، بينما يختزل النحاس الثنائي إلى نحاس."

accuracy.reason: Accurately identifies zinc as the oxidized species forming Zn2+ and Cu2+ as the reduced species forming Cu.
